enduring_promise: Turn agent intent into economical, bounded, portable, and observable execution over long-running work.
owned_seam: The mediation boundary between agent intent and model or tool execution, including the state needed to preserve that contract across turns and harnesses.
investment_principle: Emphasize the evidenced bottleneck with the highest marginal user value now; retain every must-not-regress contract when its mechanism becomes table stakes.

items.label: Performance, cache reuse, and managed context
items.why_now: Repeated model setup, prompt replay, and avoidable turns remain large, visible costs; provider cache behavior and long-session context still require active mediation.
items.retained_contract: fak must not cause avoidable repeated work and must keep efficiency claims net-true against the best real alternative.
items.increase_when: Representative tuned-baseline traces show repeated work or context reconstruction is the dominant controllable cost.
items.decrease_when: Across representative harnesses and two review cycles, tuned provider-native behavior makes fak's marginal savings immaterial and no recovery or control advantage depends on the mechanism.
items.future_state: A maintained must-not-regress efficiency invariant rather than the headline, with specialized optimization moved behind measured demand.

items.label: Harness ownership, bindings, and portable intent
items.why_now: External harness seams are fragmented and often cannot preserve context, capability, recovery, and control semantics; a working owned path is needed to prove the kernel reaches users.
items.retained_contract: At least one real path must exercise the full mediation contract, and independent bindings must preserve intent without widening capability.
items.increase_when: Integration gaps prevent the kernel's measured or bounded behavior from surviving in the harnesses users actually operate.
items.decrease_when: Two independent external bindings pass the same portable-intent, capability, session, and recovery conformance witnesses without first-party harness-specific behavior.
items.future_state: The first-party harness becomes a reference and conformance fixture; binding semantics remain central while UI and harness breadth become Enabling or Peripheral.

items.label: Fail-closed capability and effect mediation
items.why_now: Performance work already crosses the tool-call seam; enforcing a structural capability floor there prevents optimization from widening effects or relying on model persuasion.
items.retained_contract: Every mediated effect is checked before execution and ambiguous authority fails closed, regardless of which mechanism or model implements the decision.
items.increase_when: New autonomous effects, delegation, or remote execution enlarge the authority exposed through the seam.
items.decrease_when: Never as an implementation priority merely because the floor is quiet; only an explicit product-identity change that stops mediating effects can remove this contract.
items.future_state: Stable infrastructure and conformance evidence rather than necessarily the buying headline.

items.label: Model routing and bounded adaptation
items.why_now: Capability, cost, latency, and availability vary materially across calls and providers, so whole-session model pinning leaves controllable value unused.
items.retained_contract: Adaptation must remain bounded, inspectable, reversible, and correctness-preserving.
items.increase_when: Cross-model heterogeneity creates a measured end-to-end advantage after routing and evaluation overhead.
items.decrease_when: Provider-native routing meets fak's correctness, cost, inspectability, portability, and operator-control contract on representative workloads.
items.future_state: A policy and observability contract over provider routing, with custom routing retained only where it produces witnessed marginal value.

items.label: Local inference and compute backends
items.why_now: Local execution can supply privacy, availability, cost, and control for particular users, but backend breadth is not itself the product outcome.
items.retained_contract: Execution substrates remain replaceable beneath the mediation seam and are judged on full-path value.
items.increase_when: A named user path requires local privacy, availability, latency, or economics that hosted alternatives cannot meet.
items.decrease_when: Maintaining a backend costs more than its witnessed user-path advantage or equivalent controlled execution is available elsewhere.
items.future_state: Optional substrates with explicit support envelopes, not permanent Core breadth.

items.label: Evidence, observability, recovery, and operator control
items.why_now: An invisible optimization or adaptation cannot be trusted, priced, recovered, or distinguished from task failure in long-running operation.
items.retained_contract: Every material kernel decision and claimed gain remains attributable, recoverable where promised, and inspectable at the operating boundary.
items.increase_when: Autonomy, session duration, or adaptation grows faster than operators can explain and recover behavior.
items.decrease_when: Individual instrumentation mechanisms may recede after the contract is provided reliably by a lower layer; the inspectability and recovery contract does not recede.
items.future_state: A stable operational contract whose implementation follows the active bottleneck.

items.label: Fleet, dispatch, CI, release, and portfolio machinery
items.why_now: The repository's scale and concurrency create real delivery obligations, but internal operating intensity is not external product centrality.
items.retained_contract: The product remains buildable, releasable, and honestly evidenced without project machinery consuming disproportionate capacity.
items.increase_when: A measured delivery or reliability bottleneck blocks a named product spine or required obligation.
items.decrease_when: The named bottleneck clears, usage falls, or maintenance exceeds avoided delivery cost; then freeze, simplify, merge, or retire the mechanism.
items.future_state: The smallest reliable stewardship layer, with successful one-off machinery removed from strategic identity.
